packets.responsibility: Keeps Paper.js's view.viewSize (canvas.width/height, the backing resolution) in sync with the #canvas-area container's actual CSS box, via a ResizeObserver plus a window resize listener — Paper's own `resize` attribute on the canvas can get stuck at whatever size the container happened to have the instant paper.setup() ran (before the app's flex layout settled) and never recover on a later resize.
behavior: Line 41: blank line (the first line of this scope, immediately after C06's paper.setup() call at line 40).

14-line lead-in comment (42-57): reported directly by the user as a resize bug; also the root cause behind the Rust-engine mirror (engine-bridge.js) computing wrong world coordinates for an intercepted tool's live preview, since it derives its own canvas size from the same stuck view.viewSize value. A ResizeObserver is more reliable than Paper's own listener because it fires for ANY container size change (window resize, side-panel drag-resize, etc.); assigning view.viewSize directly is the documented Paper.js way to recompute the canvas's backing resolution without touching zoom/center, so only the visible viewport area changes on a resize, matching what the `resize` attribute was always supposed to do.

`syncCanvasSize()` (58-64): reads #canvas-area's clientWidth/clientHeight (59-60); if both are positive AND either dimension differs (rounded) from the current view.viewSize (61), assigns `view.viewSize=new Size(w,h)` (62) — a no-op guard so an unrelated repaint doesn't thrash Paper's own resize machinery every call.

ResizeObserver wiring (65): `if(window.ResizeObserver)new ResizeObserver(syncCanvasSize).observe(document.getElementById('canvas-area'));` — feature-detected, no fallback if the browser lacks ResizeObserver (none needed, since the resize listener below still covers the window-resize case).

Resize listener wiring (66): `window.addEventListener('resize',syncCanvasSize);` — a second, independent trigger (window-level resize, not container-level), covering the case a ResizeObserver might miss or as a redundant safety net.

packets.responsibility: Two module-global pixel constants mirroring the timeline's own CSS custom properties (--fc and .lrow/.frow/.fc's height) — every click/drag position computation in timeline.js is derived from these, so a mismatch here silently desyncs ALL timeline pointer math from what is actually on screen.
behavior: 8-line lead-in comment (68-75): confirmed real historical bug cited directly — FC was left at the old value 14 after the CSS --fc custom property moved to 16 in a redesign pass, producing a growing left-right drift the further right the user clicked/dragged in the timeline. The two constants must be kept in lockstep with style.css BY HAND — there is no single source of truth shared between CSS and JS in this codebase.
